method: Read retained git objects only; no dispatch, provider call, publication, test execution or source edit.

workflow.trigger: Push to ci/provider-readback-amazon-v1 or ci/provider-readback-cj-v1; no workflow_dispatch inputs
workflow.credentialBinding: References VERIFY_CJ_API_KEY protected environment secret; availability and account authority not examined
workflow.restrictions: First run attempt only, read-only repository permission,5minute job limit, pinned actions/runtime, fixed50point CJ bound, no application startup

actualCjPlan: Authentication exchange followed by fixed GET /product/list?pageNum=1&pageSize=1. Supported direct-token code path performs that same fixed catalog GET, but workflow does not select direct-token mode.
missingOperations: Selected CJ product detail by pid
amazonPlan: First pageSize1 seller listings observation in US marketplace; no selected ASIN or selected CJ match input. Not a matched-product qualification read.
testsReviewed: Offline tests cover fixed allowlists, failure behavior, no retry, sanitization, credential-format rejection and explicit non-qualification flags. Tests do not claim exact detail/stock/freight support. Not rerun.
scopeConclusion: Credible protected job infrastructure exists, but this retained workflow hardcodes a one-row catalogue observation rather than the currently required exact product/variant reads. Executing it would spend a provider read without closing the Q exact-interface gap.
minimalNextProof: An already existing reviewed exact-ID job implementation and its trusted invocation contract must be identified before any dispatch proposal. Otherwise adding exact detail/stock/freight is a new reviewed engineering and exact-tree publication scope, not an available execution action. Current remote branch identity, environment approval and secret/account binding would also need proof before execution.
